target.founder: Sam Mendel (CEO; serial founder, prior exit of a creator-hiring marketplace), Eric Kim (CTO; ex-Palantir, Merge; Cornell)

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $1M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
NetworkOcean is a Seed-stage company operating in Ocean & Maritime technology, founded by Sam Mendel (serial founder with prior marketplace exit) and Eric Kim (ex-Palantir, Merge; Cornell). The company has raised $1M to date. The comp universe consists of three private peers in the sector—Standard Subsea, Clippership, and Albacore—with no direct public comparables available for triangulation.

Given the early stage and limited data density, only Stage-Progression methodology proved applicable. Using $1M in total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A advancement, this method yields $2.5M. No revenue multiples, DCF, or private market precedent transactions could be calibrated with the available data.

The triangulated valuation range is $2.0M–$3.0M, with a median of $2.5M. This range reflects modest upside from the capital deployed, consistent with Seed-stage risk and founder pedigree. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue or unit economics, limited comp transparency in the maritime frontier-tech sector, and insufficient deal flow data to establish reliable stage-based benchmarks. A fuller analysis would require customer traction, TAM validation, or recent peer fundraising terms.
